doc.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: On the road with Jimmy Reed in 1957 and the moonshine
summary: He recalls touring Florida with Jimmy Reed and tricking him into quitting moonshine, and says blues lyrics come from real life.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, and “The Big Boss Man,” I think, too. But she used to be, see I went on the road with Jimmy Reed in 1957, all down in Florida, and Jimmy Reed used to drink a lot of moonshine. During this period, people were dying of drinking moonshine. So we were trying to quit Jimmy Reed from drinking. So we got this newspaper. And Jimmy Reed, when he’d get to a city, he’d get him like a gallon of this white lightning. And I mean this stuff was so strong, it would, like if you’d drink it your lips would get chapped. So, and so we started, I’d read these things out loud. Yeah. Twelve people die in Okeechobee, Mississippi, drinking this moonshine and stuff. Then we’d turn the radio on and so like we’d see Jimmy throwing his moonshine out the window. So I’m just saying, you know, there are so many different type things that happen on the road that that’s really, well that’s how you get your lyrics for songs and stuff. And these things are about life and things that really happen in people’s lives, you know.
That gives the music a certain sense of authenticity.
